body_site.evidence_quote: faecal samples collected over a period of two to four months

country.evidence_quote: Luxembourg Centre for Systems Biomedicine, Luxembourg

age_years.notes: Age data referenced in Supplementary Table 1; specific values not provided in main text.

bmi.notes: BMI referenced in Supplementary Table 1 and Methods but values not provided in main text.

dietary_restriction.notes: Specific dietary restrictions not reported; diets of individuals with T1DM matched those of healthy family members.

disease.evidence_quote: four families with multiple cases of type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM). T1DM was in all cases diagnosed

disease.notes: Inferred individual disease status from pedigree (Figure 1a); filled symbols indicate T1DM, empty symbols indicate healthy family members.

disease_details.notes: T1DM cases were long-standing (>5 years) and well-controlled with insulin therapy.

biomarker_name.notes: Multiple biomarkers identified at different omic levels (metagenomic, metatranscriptomic, metaproteomic).

biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: Relative protein abundances of human AMY2A and AMY2B; metatranscriptomic normalized reads; transcript levels
biomarker_unit.section: Methods — Protein liquid chromatography and mass spectrometry; Results
biomarker_unit.notes: Units vary by biomarker type and measurement level.

value: Thiazole synthase: correlated with AMY2 abundance (24 significant correlations, |Spearman's ρ| > 0.75)
Glycolysis genes: correlated with amylase abundance
One highly active Clostridiales mOTU: more abundant in metatranscriptomes of T1DM individuals (FDR-adjusted P < 0.05, fold change >2)
biomarker_value.evidence_quote: Pancreatic enzymes less abundant; LTF and ITLN1 higher in T1DM; 24 correlations between microbial transcripts and amylases after FDR adjustment
biomarker_value.section: Results — Human protein excretion in T1DM and microbial functions; Results — Family-independent effects of T1DM
biomarker_value.notes: Values summarize differential findings between T1DM and healthy individuals. Not all comparisons reached statistical significance after FDR adjustment.

disease_response_os.notes: This is a case study of familial T1DM examining microbiome composition and function; overall survival was not a measured outcome.

disease_response_os_unit.notes: Not applicable; no survival data reported.

ecog_performance_status.notes: Not applicable; this is a microbiome and metabolic study of families with T1DM, not an oncology trial.

value: Microbial taxonomic composition (43 ± 14% unassigned to phylum)
Functional profiles linked to metabolic traits
Human protein profiles (200 ± 70 human proteins per sample)
feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: Faecal samples collected over two to four months; mOTU-based taxonomic profiles stable over time; 53 well-preserved samples; 2,400 ± 1,600 microbial and 200 ± 70 human protein groups per sample
feces_phenotype_value.section: Study cohort and microbial community structures; Integrated multi-omics
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Multiple phenotype measurements from fecal samples at different omic levels. Samples collected at three time points (visits 1, 2, 3).

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Not applicable; this study does not involve tumor measurement.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Not applicable; this is not an oncology study.

value: Study design: observational case study of four purposely selected family groups with at least two members with T1DM
Cohort: 20 individuals from four families of at least two generations
T1DM status: diagnosed for more than five years, successfully controlled by insulin replacement therapy
Healthy relatives: auto-antibody status did not indicate immediate risk of developing T1DM
Sample collection: three time points at intervals of 4-8 weeks
Metagenomic sequencing: 3.9 ± 0.1 Gbp per sample, 101 bp paired-end reads on HiSeq2000
Metatranscriptomic sequencing: 8.0 ± 1.0 Gbp per sample, 150 bp paired-end reads, rRNA-depleted
Metaproteomic analysis: 185,000 ± 13,000 peptide mass spectra per sample
Co-assembly: 287 ± 43 Mbp total assembled genomic contigs; N50: 660 ± 130 bp
Gene annotations: 489,000 ± 75,000 predicted ORFs with functional categories (KEGG, MetaCyc, Swiss-Prot)
Non-human eukaryotic biomolecules: 0.07 ± 0.05% of metagenomic reads, 0.8 ± 1% of metatranscriptomic reads, 2.6 ± 3.1% of proteins
Viral biomolecules: <0.1% of predicted ORFs and mappable reads
mOTU abundance correlation (metaG vs metaT): Spearman's ρ = 0.81 ± 0.15; P < 2.2 × 10−16
mOTU-ORF coverage correlation: Spearman's ρ = 0.06 ± 0.09 (weak overall)
Functional profile correlation (metaG vs metaT): Spearman's ρ = 0.41 ± 0.08; P < 2.2 × 10−16
Protein-transcript correlation (metaT vs metaP): Spearman's ρ = 0.40 ± 0.16 (functional category-wise); P < 2.2 × 10−16
Family membership effect: pronounced effect on structural and functional composition of microbiota
T1DM-specific findings: no consistent taxonomic differences across families; lower exocrine pancreatic protein levels
Thiamine blood levels: low levels linked to T1DM complications; colonic uptake transporters described; patterns not correlated in small supplement-free subset
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: 20 individuals from four families; T1DM diagnosed for more than five years; insulin replacement therapy; three visits 4-8 weeks apart; 53 faecal samples; 3.9 ± 0.1 Gbp metagenomic data; 8.0 ± 1.0 Gbp metatranscriptomic data; 185,000 ± 13,000 mass spectra
uncurated_metadata.section: Study cohort and microbial community structures; Methods; Integrated multi-omics
uncurated_metadata.notes: Comprehensive metadata including sequencing parameters, assembly statistics, sample collection procedures, and key findings from multi-omic integration.

host_species.evidence_quote: Study of four families with familial type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM); human blood and faecal samples; whole human genome sequencing
host_species.section: Abstract; Methods — Anthropometric, nutritional, clinical data and blood and stool sampling
host_species.notes: The paper studies human families with type 1 diabetes. Human genome sequencing and blood/stool collection confirm human subjects.
